correctness.rationale: The proof counts cyclic transitions of each nonconstant affine evaluation word from the precise binary carry structure. The affine-mask-to-prefix-parity map is bijective and gives every possible zero-run count with exact multiplicity. Nonzero low-bit restrictions ensure no all-zero window of length \(2^s+1\); low-bit-zero words are stretched balanced affine words, for which all-zero windows are enumerated exactly by zero runs. This handles wrap-around, constants, all ranges and both coordinate orderings. Direct exhaustive codeword/window enumeration for m=2..9 agrees at every claimed width; the proof, not finite data, establishes the infinite family.

value.rationale: The first-order Reed–Muller family is a canonical low-rate affine evaluation code, and cyclic b-symbol weight captures an operationally distinct overlapping-read metric sensitive to coordinate order. Natural dyadic-plus-one windows align with the code’s recursive block structure. The theorem gives the full distribution for an infinite family, a constant interior multiplicity law, all exact positive weight levels, and the exact minimum, which generic cardinality or Hamming-weight results do not determine.
